market_holds: Spot about $15.6-16.1 (sealed 15.565 at 18:08 UTC; Yahoo intraday 16.09 on 11-17). The stock is -9.7% over 5 days, -16.5% over 20 days and -40.7% from its 52-week high: it closed at 26.25 on 2026-08-27 after the Q2 rally and has fallen steadily since, through a risk-off tape (QQQ 715 to 654 from 10-29 to 11-17). There is no usable option chain (ATM spread 192% of mid). The usual move: print-day closes were +13.7% (2025-09-12), -3.6% (2025-11-10), -7.7% (2026-02-18), -8.0% (2026-06-10) and +0.2% (2026-08-18), median absolute about 7.7%; 20-day realised vol is 74%. Consensus per Yahoo earningsTrend (9 analysts, read 2026-11-17) is the guide itself: Q3 revenue $63.21M (guide $63-64M), Q4 $78.6M (guide $75-84M total), FY26 $224.25M (guide $220-230M), FY27 $406.5M (guide $400M+). EPS estimates have been cut hard over 90 days (Q3 -0.42 to -0.90, FY -2.59 to -3.38) with no revenue cut, and ratings are 7 buy, 0 hold. Short interest is 2.98% of float (10-30). The base is retail and sentiment is promotional (a Stocktwits live-stream call). The stock trades on the IM8 monthly run-rate (the post-quarter month is disclosed in each release), the Q4/FY guide and the 2027 $400M target.
view: Q3 revenue is close to known: management guided $61.5-62.5M of IM8 on 08-18 with July ($20.9M) and part of August in hand, and it has landed at or near the guide midpoint for two quarters (Q2 IM8 $45.0M against $44-46M). The print is therefore decided by the forward line: October's number, which the release will almost certainly carry as it carried May and July, and whether Q4 at $75-81M IM8 and the 2027 $400M+ survive. The price has already lost 40% while revenue consensus has not moved, so the market already disbelieves the guide. The traces I can see partly justify that doubt. (1) A company that announced every record month (May, June, July) has published no monthly figure since July. Its 11-03, 11-05 and 11-16 releases still cite July's $251M run rate. (2) The CFO tendered his resignation on 10-30 'to pursue new opportunities' (6-K 11-02, stock -7% that day), a month after quarter-end; the company recast it the next day as a planned succession. (3) IM8 Hydration slid from 'launches in Q4 2026' (Q2 shareholder letter, 08-18) to 'Q1 of 2027' (Diplo release, 11-16). (4) Google search interest for the brand is flat since May and soft in October ('IM8' US monthly average Jul 61.8, Sep 64.0, Oct 53.3, Nov 50.0; 'im8 health' worldwide Jul 50.2, Oct 19.5). That is not the acceleration a +21-31% sequential Q4 needs. Against this: the 11-16 release, written with October closed, restates the FY $220-230M guide, so a FY cut is less likely than the tape implies. About 40% of July's record cohort chose quarterly plans, which are recognised on shipment, so October carries the quarterly renewal bulge and will likely print as a record 'run-rate' headline. And the stock is already washed out. Net: a slight lean down, from a mid-session fade on print days (close below open in 4 of 5 recent prints) and from soft forward demand traces, but nowhere near the confidence needed to bet.

recommendation.reason: The soft traces (no monthly records since July, the CFO resignation, the Hydration slip, flat brand search) point to a Q4 guide at risk. But the price has already fallen 40% on exactly that doubt, while the FY guide was restated publicly two days before the print with October known. I cannot show that the doubt is under-priced rather than fully priced, so there is no bet.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An October IM8 revenue figure well above July's $20.9M (for example $24M or more) with Q4 and the 2027 $400M+ reaffirmed would favour a relief rally from a washed-out price; a Q4 or FY guide cut would make the move down large.

self_critique: The strongest case for up: revenue consensus sits exactly on a guide the company restated two days before the print with October known, and this company has hit its guide twice running. October will probably carry the quarterly-renewal bulge and headline as a record run rate. After a 40% slide, a promotional retail-heavy name can squeeze sharply on any reaffirmation; the Q2 print started a 35% rally within a week. The Google Trends terms are low-volume and ambiguous ('IM8' is not unique), and most IM8 acquisition comes through paid social, not search, so my main demand trace is weak.
approach_notes: Freshest-data-first and 'read the company's own later releases' paid: the Hydration slip and the unchanged July ARR in the 11-16 release were only visible in the primary exhibits. P4's 'priced in is a claim to prove' cut both ways here: the consensus is provably on the guide, but the 40% price slide shows the doubt is priced, so I had no clean gap to bet on.
